name: Warsong Outrider Update
summary: Along eastern Ashenvale, the Warsong Outrider Update carries word of danger closing in on the Horde. Its report names Alliance forces, satyr entrenched in the forest, and naga moving through neighboring Azshara.

sections.title: Eyes Along the Forest Edge
sections.body: A lone Warsong Outrider watches Ashenvale’s contested eastern edge. Horde supply lines face constant harassment, so outriders track enemy movements before raiding parties can strike Mor'shan Rampart or Splintertree Post. Meet one on patrol and you know the forest is under watch. His report may decide whether a Horde fortification holds or falls to ambush.

sections.title: Threats on Every Horizon
sections.body: A Warsong Outrider’s report tells of danger across Kalimdor’s central forests. Night elves and the wider Alliance remain a threat, while cunning, demonic satyr haunt eastern Ashenvale. Scouts have also found a massive naga presence spreading through the ruined coastal lands of neighboring Azshara. The Horde faces hostile powers from nearly every direction.

faq.answer: The Warsong Report is an intelligence dispatch from a Warsong Outrider about enemy positions and dangers in the region. It names nearby Alliance forces, active satyr covens in eastern Ashenvale, and newly discovered naga movements across Azshara.

Kadrak is a Horde commander stationed at Mor'shan Rampart, the defensive barricade guarding the northern border between the Barrens and Ashenvale. He oversees incoming scouts and coordinates forward operations into the forest.

faq.q: Why are the naga in Azshara mentioned?
faq.answer: Azshara borders eastern Ashenvale, and naga movements there could threaten the Horde’s flank. Outriders watch nearby lands so the Horde is not surprised by a massive incursion while facing the night elves.

faq.q: What makes eastern Ashenvale so dangerous for the Horde?
faq.answer: In eastern Ashenvale, the Horde faces active Alliance detachments, ancient ruins filled with demonic corruption and satyr, and untamed woodland beasts. Couriers and patrols risk ambush from every direction.
The Warsong Outriders are the Warsong clan’s forward vanguard and reconnaissance cavalry in Ashenvale. They track night elf movements, screen logging camps, and secure trade roads.

faq.q: Why can't the outrider deliver the report himself?
faq.answer: The outrider must watch the trail and track hostile movements as they develop. If he leaves his vantage point, the frontline could miss an unexpected Alliance or satyr advance.

angles.text: As a member of the Horde, you know every dispatch along the Mor'shan line matters to the Horde’s fragile foothold in Ashenvale’s forests.
As an orc, you know the Warsong clan takes pride in holding the vanguard. Its scouts also know bravery alone cannot stop enemies closing in from every side.
